unsupported_claims: Evaluated datasets include Twitter and Sina Weibo-type networks (the paper uses Wikipedia language network, Flickr, YouTube, and DBLP citation networks).
Datasets include 'some smaller benchmark networks' (the paper says each network has at least half a million nodes).
Costs are roughly quadratic memory and cubic time (the paper only says time complexity is at least quadratic in the number of vertices and mentions eigendecomposition).
rationale: The core reason (these methods do not scale to networks of this size) is supported, as is the millions-of-vertices to billions-of-edges scale. However, the answer invents specific datasets (Twitter, Sina Weibo), smaller benchmark networks that contradict 'each at least half a million nodes', and specific memory/time complexities not in the evidence.
